title: Unsafe Type Casting and Type Confusion
platform_conditions: C++11 and later on any conforming toolchain; RTTI-based dynamic_cast requires the base class to be polymorphic (at least one virtual function)
security_mechanism: static_cast<Derived*>(base_ptr) converts the pointer with zero runtime information: if the object is actually a different derived type (or a base), every subsequent member access through the resulting pointer computes offsets for the wrong layout, so a field write lands inside another field — classic type confusion that turns an object of one attacker-influenced type into another. reinterpret_cast and C-style casts are stronger still, permitting pointer-type punning and integer/pointer round-trips that violate strict aliasing. Unions used for type punning read a member of type T from bytes written as type U, which is undefined behavior the compiler may optimize across.

source_sink_clues.source: Type tags, discriminator fields, or polymorphic handles that arrive from deserialized data, plugin registries, or protocol payloads and then drive a downcast.
source_sink_clues.sink: static_cast / reinterpret_cast / C-style cast to a derived or unrelated pointer type on data whose dynamic type is attacker-influenced; union member reads of a different active member

tracking_guards: Check that polymorphic downcasts use dynamic_cast with a null-result check (requires RTTI enabled), that any tag-driven cast validates the tag against the concrete object (e.g. via a virtual type id comparison that also fails closed), and that data reinterpretation goes through bit_cast (C++20) or explicit serialization rather than union punning.
not_candidate_when: The object's dynamic type is guaranteed by construction (factory that only produces Derived) and documented with an assertion, dynamic_cast with failure handling replaces the static_cast, or the cast is between layout-compatible numeric types with no object reuse.
public_references: CWE-704: Incorrect Type Conversion or Cast — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/704.html
CWE-843: Access of Resource Using Incompatible Type ('Type Confusion') — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/843.html
